stage_2_story.text_en:
Every Friday, Avi and his wife do a deep clean of the house before Shabbat. They divide the rooms between them and work together until everything is spotless.

Avi always starts with the floors. First he takes the broom and sweeps through the entire apartment — the hallway, the kitchen, and the living room. He collects all the dust and crumbs into the dustpan and empties it into the bin. Then he fills a bucket with hot water and adds a small amount of detergent. He dips the mop in, wrings it out, and goes over every floor carefully.

For the bathrooms, Avi uses bleach. He pours it around the toilet bowl and along the edges of the sink, lets it sit for a few minutes, then scrubs with a stiff brush. The tiles on the walls he wipes down with a damp sponge, working from top to bottom so the dirty water drips down.

Meanwhile, his wife handles the bedrooms. She runs the vacuum over all the carpets and rugs, and uses a dry cloth to wipe the dust off the shelves and furniture.

When Avi finishes the bathrooms, he rinses his tools under the tap, hangs the mop to dry, and puts everything back in the cleaning cupboard. The whole process takes about two hours. By midday, the apartment is clean and fresh. Avi makes coffee and they sit together at the kitchen table. "Same time next week," Miriam always says with a smile.
